Exact conditional Poisson regression (fast, closed-form algorithm)

Source: R/ep-closed-form.R
ep_closed_form.Rd

Computes the exact conditional maximum likelihood estimate, exact confidence interval, and exact p-value for the coefficient of a single two-level (treatment vs. control) factor in a Poisson regression with log offset and, optionally, one or more stratification variables acting purely as nuisance intercepts. This is the special case handled by ep_multi_shift() when the model contains exactly one exact effect with two levels and no other categorical covariates; in that special case, the exact distribution can be obtained in closed form, stratum by stratum, following Guess, Lydick, Small and Miller (1987) and Guess and Thomas (1990), instead of by the general per-observation network algorithm. See the accompanying theory note for why this is faster in this scenario, and use ep_multi_shift() whenever the model contains additional categorical covariates to adjust for, or more than one exact effect.

ep_closed_form(
  formula,
  data,
  offset = NULL,
  offset_log = TRUE,
  strata = NULL,
  ref_levels = list(),
  alpha = 0.05,
  ci_type = c("two-sided", "one-sided"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula of the form response ~ group, where group is the two-level factor of interest and is the formula's only right-hand-side term. Strata and the offset are supplied separately (as in ep_multi_shift()), not as terms in this formula.

data

A data frame. One row per observation; rows belonging to the same stratum and the same level of group are summed internally, so data may be individual-level or already aggregated.

offset

Name of the person-time / exposure variable in data, or NULL (default). If NULL, every observation is treated as contributing one unit of exposure (offset = 0 on the log scale), matching ep_multi_shift(). Note that, unlike the general algorithms, supplying offset here never imposes a per-observation cap on any observation's count (see Details).

offset_log

If TRUE (default, matching ep_multi_shift()), offset already holds log(exposure). If FALSE, offset holds raw exposure and is logged internally.

strata

Optional character vector naming one or more stratification variables in data. If NULL (default), all observations form a single stratum, i.e. an unstratified two-sample exact Poisson test.

ref_levels

Optional named list giving the reference (control) level of the formula's group variable, e.g. list(trt = "0"); the other level is treated as the treatment group. Defaults to R's usual first level.

alpha

Type I error rate for the confidence interval (default 0.05).

ci_type

"two-sided" or "one-sided".

verbose

If TRUE (default), prints a short note identifying this as the closed-form two-group/strata-only algorithm.

Value

An object of class c("ep_closed_form", "ep_fit"): a list with elements exactparmest (a one-row data frame with Parameter, Estimate (the coefficient beta = log rate ratio, not the rate ratio), StdError, Alpha, LowerCL, UpperCL (beta scale), PValue, and SuffStat), OUTDIST (the exact distribution of the sufficient statistic), and call.

Details

Unlike ep_multi_shift() and ep_network(), this function has no exactmax argument and never imposes a per-observation cap beyond what conditioning on the stratum total already implies (SAS's own "Rule 2"; see the theory vignette, Sections 5.2 and 10). In particular, supplying offset here does not trigger the offset-implied per-observation cap ("Rule 3": \(S_i = \max(\lceil e^{o_i} \rceil, 1)\)) that the general algorithms apply automatically whenever offset is supplied without exactmax. When that cap would bind, small exposures relative to the observed counts, typically in unstratified or lightly-stratified two-group data, ep_closed_form() and the general algorithms are, by design, answering subtly different questions, and can legitimately disagree on the estimate, confidence interval, and p-value even given identical call arguments. This is expected, documented behaviour, not a bug in either algorithm; see the theory vignette for a worked numerical example and tests/testthat/test-cross-algorithm-agreement.R for a regression test that locks in the expected divergence.

References

Guess HA, Lydick EG, Small RD, Miller LP, Exact binomial confidence intervals for the relative risk in follow-up studies with sparsely stratified incidence density data, American Journal of Epidemiology, Volume 125, Issue 2, February 1987, Pages 340-347, https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a114535

Guess HA, Thomas JE. A rapidly converging algorithm for exact binomial confidence intervals about the relative risk in follow-up studies with stratified incidence-density data. Epidemiology. 1990 Jan;1(1):75-7. doi: 10.1097/00001648-199001000-00016. PMID: 2081244.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  cases  = c(3, 32, 1, 19, 2, 24, 4, 40),
  fu     = c(100, 100, 120, 120, 150, 150, 170, 170),
  trt    = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0),
  strata = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4)
)
ep_closed_form(
  formula    = cases ~ trt,
  data       = df,
  offset     = "fu",
  offset_log = FALSE,
  strata     = "strata"
)
#> 
#> Closed-form two-group/strata-only exact Poisson algorithm
#>                 (Guess & Thomas, 1990): 4 stratum(strata), 10 treatment cases,
#>                 115 control cases.
#> 
#> Exact conditional Poisson, two groups + strata (closed-form Guess & Thomas algorithm)
#> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#>  Parameter  Estimate  StdError Alpha   LowerCL   UpperCL      PValue SuffStat
#>       trt1 -2.442347 0.3296902  0.05 -3.203615 -1.797111 9.11799e-24       10
